newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ COACH TIPS FRANCE AS TEAM TO BEAT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ COACH TIPS FRANCE AS TEAM TO BEAT.

text.p: All Black coach John Hart said on Monday that Five Nations champions France could be the team to beat at the 1999 rugby World Cup.
Speaking on breakfast television after New Zealand's 55-35 thrashing of South Africa at the weekend, Hart said he believed the All Blacks could be beaten.
"I think any side in Australia, South Africa, France on any given day could beat the All Blacks, if the All Blacks aren't on song," he said.
"I believe that France could be the side to beat in the '99 World Cup," he added.

The All Blacks have won all seven of their test matches this year, and their drubbing of World Cup holders South Africa by a record winning margin leaves them a clear notch above the rest in many people's minds.
They have not played France yet, however, and in an end-of-year tour of Europe are scheduled to play only England, Ireland and Wales.
But Hart said the difference between the world's top sides was not as great as some observers imagined.
He said political wrangling in South African rugby was the main cause of the Springboks' dismal form this year and the world champions would recover.

"I think you'll see a total resurgence in South African rugby. There's great qualities there, they just need to get their coaching and administration right. I think politics wrecks their game at the moment, and if they get that right, watch out," he said.
"So in the next few years I think Australia, South Africa, France and England too, if they get their attitude to the game right, all those sides could beat the All Blacks."
The All Blacks next play Australia at Dunedin on Saturday. If they win New Zealand will secure the Tri-Nations championship for the second year in succession.
